15.0.s.en: (1) The portion of the tribe of Judah

15.0.0.en: According to their families: it includes all the families of the tribe.

15.0.3.en: The Salt Sea: the Dead Sea.

15.0.4.en: Joshua began the distribution of the land from the south to the north, and it was done by lot. God chose the tribe of Judah as the first of the tribes in the lot because it was the most pious of the tribes, and from it Christ came forth; the Temple was in its land, and its kingship lasted longer than that of the other tribes, so it went into captivity as the last of the tribes.

15.0.5.en: The borders of Judah were very wide, and these verses include the southern borders of the tribe of Judah, which is the country of Edom, the descendants of Esau, who lived in the mountains of Seir, and “the wilderness of Zin,” which adjoins the mountains of Seir and lies on the southern border of the land of Judah. The border of Judah extends to the farthest, that is, the last part of the Dead Sea in the south, which is a bay (Map 8). The border extended southward to “the ascent of Akrabbim”; ascent means a rough road on the mountain, and Akrabbim means scorpions, and it was called so because of the many scorpions in it. Beyond it to the west is the wilderness of Zin, which is part of the wilderness of Paran extending north of the wilderness of Sinai.

15.0.6.en: It passes south of Kadesh-barnea, then reaches a village called Hezron beside Kadesh-barnea, and goes up to a neighboring village higher than it called Addar, then turns to a low part in the wilderness of Zin called Karkaa, then reaches Azmon, which is northwest of the wilderness of Sinai, then passes beside the river of Egypt, meaning the Wadi al-Arish, which is the valley of a seasonal river that fills with rain in the rainy season and flows into the Mediterranean Sea. What is meant by the goings out of the border is the end of the southern border of the tribe of Judah, which is the sea, that is, the Mediterranean Sea. So the southern border extends east from the south of the Dead Sea and extends west to the Mediterranean Sea.

15.1.0.en: This verse tells us of the eastern border of the tribe of Judah, which is the Dead Sea, that is, “the Salt Sea,” to its end in the north, that is, at the mouth of the Jordan River into it.

15.1.1.en: In this verse he also begins to make clear the northern border of the tribe of Judah, which begins from the tongue, that is, the bay that lies north of the Dead Sea and into which the Jordan River flows, that is, the uttermost part of the Jordan.

15.2.0.en: He continues the northern border of the tribe of Judah. The border passes by Beth-hogla, which lies east of Jericho, then passes through a plain called Beth-arabah, then the stone of Bohan, then passes the valley of Achor, which lies south of Jericho and was so named because of the sin of Achan the son of Carmi, and after that reaches the village of Debir, which is Kirjath-sepher (v. 15). After that the border turns north to reach “Gilgal,” where the tabernacle of meeting was set up and which was the headquarters of Joshua the son of Nun. Gilgal is opposite a region called “the going up to Adummim,” which separates the borders of Judah and Benjamin, and it passes south of a valley that separates Judah and Benjamin. Then it passes the waters of En-shemesh, a spring of water lying three miles east of Jerusalem and separating the borders of Judah and Benjamin. Then the border reaches its farthest point at En-rogel, which lies near Jerusalem and also separates the land of Judah and Benjamin. Then it turns to the valley of the son of Hinnom, which lies southwest of Jerusalem. The Jebusite means the Jebusites, the original inhabitants of Jerusalem. Then the border goes up on the mountain that lies opposite the region in which the Rephaim live, a people of giants among the original inhabitants of the land, and perhaps this mountain is Mount Zion, which lies beside Jerusalem.

15.2.1.en: Then the border extends to the well of Nephtoah, which is on the border of Judah and Benjamin, then to Mount Ephron, which is also on the border of Judah and Benjamin. After that it extends to the village of Baalah, which is Kirjath-jearim, and the Gibeonites lived in it (ch. 9:17). Then it extends to Mount Seir, then to Mount Jearim, then to Beth-shemesh and Timnah, all on the northern border of Judah.

15.2.2.en: Then it extends to Mount Ekron and from it to Shicron, then across Mount Baalah, and from it to the city of Jabneel, which lies 6 km east of the Mediterranean Sea and was a center of learning, where the highest assembly of the Jews, that is, the Sanhedrin, met. Then the border extends to reach the Mediterranean Sea.

15.3.0.en: The western border of Judah is the Mediterranean Sea.

15.3.1.en: Keep borders for your life that you do not overstep to take the rights of others, so that you respect their right not only in material things but also in speech and conduct. In this way you live in peace with others and hurt no one's feelings.

15.4.s.en: (2) Caleb's portion in the midst of Judah

15.4.0.en: Caleb took his portion directly, before and outside the lot, according to the commandment of Moses the prophet. As explained earlier, he took Kirjath-arba the father of Anak, which is Hebron, and the mountain with its caves (ch. 14:12).

15.5.0.en: With strong faith Caleb drove out the Anakim with their three families.

15.6.0.en: Caleb came to the village of Kirjath-sepher, and promised that whoever drove its inhabitants out of it, he would give him his daughter Achsah as a wife. It is understood from this that many young men wished to be joined to his daughter, and he wanted to marry her to the one among them most courageous, most able to bear responsibility, and most loving of God.

15.7.0.en: Othniel took the city of Debir, so Caleb gave him his daughter Achsah as a wife. Othniel was probably Caleb's brother or his brother's son, and Othniel became one of the judges of the children of Israel and delivered his people from the Aramaeans (Judg 3:8-11).

15.8.0.en: As she came to him: when she was being brought in procession to her bridegroom on her way to her new home.

15.8.1.en: She moved him: she encouraged him and urged him on.

15.8.2.en: The upper springs and the nether springs: springs that flow from high lands and from low lands.

15.8.3.en: During the wedding procession of Achsah the daughter of Caleb, before she reached her home, she encouraged her husband to ask a blessing from her father, and it seems that he was shy, so she came forward to ask this blessing from her father herself, which was the request for a field. Although she did not ask for a new piece of land, she asked for springs to water the lands that she and her husband had possessed, which are worthless if there are no sources of water to irrigate them; with this water she would have acquired a field. Note her respect for her father: she got down from the donkey she was riding on her way to her home and asked her father for this blessing, and he gave it to her (Judg 1:8-15).

15.8.4.en: Everyone who asks finds, and to him who knocks it is opened. Ask God to change your weaknesses into strength, and He will give and will not reproach. Just as Achsah asked from her father, ask from your heavenly Father, and trust in His fatherhood and love that He will give you all your needs.

15.9.s.en: (3) The cities in the portion of Judah

15.9.0.en: We shall mention here the cities whose location is now certain; as for the rest of the cities, there are differing opinions about their location.

15.9.1.en: The uttermost ... southward: those on the southern border of the portion of the tribe of Judah, which were beside the border of the country of Edom.

15.9.3.en: Adar: it is now Adar, which lies south of Gaza at a distance of 7.5 km.

15.9.4.en: Hazor (v. 23:) There are many places by the name of Hazor or Hezron, which means an enclosure, since enclosures for cattle were set up there.

15.9.5.en: Shema: it lies in the Negev and is now called Tell Sufa.

15.9.6.en: Beersheba: it lies about 45 km south of Galilee, and it is where Abraham made a covenant with Abimelech and sacrificed seven ewe lambs as proof of his ownership of the neighboring well (Gen 21:31). Kadesh: it is either Kadesh-barnea, from which Moses sent the spies to spy out the Promised Land (Num 13:26), or another Kadesh, since there are many cities by this name. The meaning of Kadesh is holy, since in the cities called Kadesh places for the worship of idols were set up.

15.9.7.en: Kerioth: it is the hometown of Judas Iscariot, that is, he was of the same tribe as Christ (the tribe of Judah), but he sold his Master.

15.9.8.en: Here are mentioned 38 cities lying in the south of the portion of the tribe of Judah, beside the Edomites and the Arab tribes, but the tribe of Simeon took nine cities from Judah because its own portion was too small for it (ch. 19:1-9), so the tribe of Judah was left with only 29 cities in the south.

15.9.9.en: (b) The plain region in the portion of Judah (vv. 33-47:) 33 And in the valley, Eshtaol, and Zoreah, and Ashnah, 34 And Zanoah, and Engannim, Tappuah, and Enam, 35 Jarmuth, and Adullam, Socoh, and Azekah, 36 And Sharaim, and Adithaim, and Gederah, and Gederothaim; fourteen cities with their villages: 37 Zenan, and Hadashah, and Migdalgad, 38 And Dilean, and Mizpeh, and Joktheel, 39 Lachish, and Bozkath, and Eglon, 40 And Cabbon, and Lahmam, and Kithlish, 41 And Gederoth, Bethdagon, and Naamah, and Makkedah; sixteen cities with their villages: 42 Libnah, and Ether, and Ashan, 43 And Jiphtah, and Ashnah, and Nezib, 44 And Keilah, and Achzib, and Mareshah; nine cities with their villages: 45 Ekron, with her towns and her villages: 46 From Ekron westward, all that lay near Ashdod, with their villages:

15.9.10.en: 47 Ashdod with her towns and her villages, Gaza with her towns and her villages, unto the river of Egypt, and the great sea, and the border thereof.

15.10.0.en: Eshtaol: it lies about 12 km west of Jerusalem.

15.10.1.en: Zoreah: it still has its name to this day and lies about 22.5 km west of Jerusalem.

15.10.2.en: Ashnah: it lies about 25 km northwest of Jerusalem.

15.10.4.en: The valley (v. 33): it is the low land lying in the middle of the land of Canaan.

15.10.5.en: Here are mentioned 14 cities with their villages, that is, the villages surrounding them, and they lie in the plain in the midst of the portion of Judah.

15.11.0.en: He continues the cities lying in the plain in the midst of the portion of the tribe of Judah, and mentions 16 cities with their suburbs.

15.12.0.en: Here he mentions nine cities with their villages, also lying in the middle plain in the portion of the tribe of Judah.

15.13.0.en: Ekron: one of the great Philistine cities and the seat of the god Baal-zebub; it lies about 19 km south of Joppa.

15.13.1.en: Ashdod: one of the great Philistine cities, and the seat of the god Dagon; the meaning of its name is strength or power, and it lies 18 miles northeast of Gaza.

15.13.2.en: Gaza: one of the great Philistine cities, lying near the Mediterranean Sea (ch. 13:

15.13.3.en: 3.(The river of Egypt: the valley of the seasonal river Al-Arish, which is not the valley of the Nile.

15.13.4.en: The great sea: the Mediterranean Sea.

15.13.5.en: Here are mentioned three large cities in the portion of the tribe of Judah, lying in the west of its portion toward the Mediterranean Sea.

15.13.6.en: Thus the total of the cities lying in the plain is 42 cities.

15.13.7.en: (c) The hill country in the portion of Judah (vv. 48-59:) 48 And in the mountains, Shamir, and Jattir, and Socoh, 49 And Dannah, and Kirjathsannah (which is Debir), 50 And Anab, and Eshtemoh, and Anim, 51 And Goshen, and Holon, and Giloh; eleven cities with their villages: 52 Arab, and Dumah, and Eshean, 53 And Janum, and Bethtappuah, and Aphekah, 54 And Humtah, and Kirjatharba (which is Hebron), and Zior; nine cities with their villages: 55 Maon, Carmel, and Ziph, and Juttah, 56 And Jezreel, and Jokdeam, and Zanoah, 57 Cain, Gibeah, and Timnah; ten cities with their villages: 58 Halhul, Bethzur, and Gedor, 59 And Maarath, and Bethanoth, and Eltekon; six cities with their villages.

15.14.0.en: The mountain: the high lands far from the seacoast and overlooking the valley of the Jordan River from its western bank.

15.14.1.en: Shamir: it lies 17 km west of Al-Khalil (Hebron).

15.14.2.en: Kirjath-sannah: it is Debir or Kirjath-sepher, which Othniel the son of Kenaz took (vv. 7, 15). Anab: it lies southwest of the city of Al-Khalil at a distance of 26 km.

15.14.3.en: Eshtemoh: it lies south of Al-Khalil at a distance of 15 km.

15.14.4.en: Anim: it lies south of Al-Khalil at a distance of 19 km.

15.14.5.en: The first group of the cities lying in the hill country in the lands of Judah numbers 11 cities with their villages.

15.15.0.en: Arab: it is the village of Al-Rabiya, which lies south of the city of Al-Khalil.

15.15.1.en: Dumah: it still has its name to this day and lies southwest of the city of Al-Khalil at a distance of 19 km. Eshean: beside the city of Al-Khalil.

15.15.2.en: Janum: beside Hebron, which is Al-Khalil.

15.15.3.en: Beth-tappuah: it is now called Al-Tuffah and lies eight km west of Al-Khalil.

15.15.4.en: Humtah: a village beside the city of Al-Khalil.

15.15.5.en: Kirjath-arba: it is Hebron, now called the city of Al-Khalil (ch. 10:3). Zior: it is now called the small village (Saghir) and lies eight km northeast of Al-Khalil.

15.15.6.en: The second group of the cities lying in the hill country in the lands of Judah numbers nine cities with their villages.

15.16.0.en: Maon: it lies on a hill south of the city of Al-Khalil at a distance of 13 km.

15.16.1.en: Ziph: it lies beside the wilderness of Ziph, 7 km southeast of Al-Khalil, and is different from the one mentioned in (v. 24). Juttah: it is the village of Yatta and lies about 9 km west of Al-Khalil.

15.16.2.en: Jokdeam: south of Al-Khalil, near Juttah.

15.16.4.en: Gibeah: it lies north of Al-Khalil at a distance of 16 km.

15.16.5.en: Timnah: it lies south of Al-Khalil.

15.16.6.en: The third group of the cities lying in the hill lands of Judah numbers ten cities with their villages.

15.17.0.en: Halhul: it lies about 6 km north of Al-Khalil.

15.17.1.en: Beth-zur: it lies about 7 km north of Al-Khalil and still has its name to this day.

15.17.2.en: Gedor: it lies between Hebron and Bethlehem.

15.17.3.en: Maarath: it lies about 12 km north of Al-Khalil and is different from the one mentioned in (ch. 13:4). Beth-anoth: it lies about 5 km northeast of Al-Khalil.

15.17.4.en: Eltekon: it lies about 7 km west of Bethlehem.

15.17.5.en: The fourth group of the cities lying in the hill lands of Judah numbers six cities with their villages.

15.17.6.en: (d) The wilderness region in the portion of Judah (vv. 60-63:) 60 Kirjathbaal (which is Kirjathjearim), and Rabbah; two cities with their villages. 61 In the wilderness, Betharabah, Middin, and Secacah, 62 And Nibshan, and the city of Salt, and Engedi; six cities with their villages. 63 As for the Jebusites the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the children of Judah could not drive them out: but the Jebusites dwell with the children of Judah at Jerusalem unto this day.

15.18.0.en: Kirjath-baal or Jearim: it was called by this name after Baal, the most famous of the gods of the Canaanites, and it lies about 15 km west of Jerusalem.

15.18.1.en: The fifth group of the cities lying in the hill lands of Judah numbers two cities with their villages.

15.18.2.en: Thus the total of the cities lying in the hill lands of Judah is 38 cities.

15.19.0.en: The wilderness: the wilderness (v. 61) is the wilderness of Judah west of the Dead Sea and southwest of Jerusalem, in which John the Baptist grew up (Lk 3:3), and it is called the wilderness of Judea (Mt 3:1). Nibshan: it lies southeast of Jericho.

15.19.1.en: The city of Salt: it lies close to the Dead Sea, about 13 km southwest of Jericho. Engedi: it lies a mile west of the Dead Sea, and beside it is a spring of water of the same name. The wilderness of Judea includes six cities with their villages.

15.19.2.en: From this we know that the portion of Judah includes 115 cities with their villages and fields.

15.20.0.en: The Jebusites: they are the descendants of Canaan the son of Ham, that is, one of the Canaanite tribes, and they are the original inhabitants of Jerusalem. Although Joshua had overcome them, being among the five kings (ch. 11:1-12), they came back and took possession of part of Jerusalem.

15.20.1.en: The tribe of Judah was lax in driving them out, either out of fear of them, or out of laziness on the part of the tribe of Judah, or in an attempt to use them as slaves, and the rest of the tribes fell into this negligence, which led these inhabitants to rise against the Jews and humiliate them, as appears in the Book of Judges. David overcame the Jebusites and took Jerusalem and the mountain (2 Sam 5).

15.20.2.en: Continue your striving to be rid of every source of sin, and do not be lax with the smallest thing, lest it become an opening for the devil, and trust in the power of God that supports you, so that you purify yourself from every evil inclination. The portion of the tribe of Ephraim
